findings.summary: New vim history routing (`routeVimHistoryToStore`) has no test at all
findings.evidence: `routeVimHistoryToStore()` globally replaces `CodeMirror.commands.undo/redo` so vim's `u` / `<C-r>` hit the store, including a read-only/facet-missing fallthrough branch. The only vim test in the diff-adjacent suite is editor.test.ts:156 'switches the keybinding mode', which only asserts `getKeymap()` and text preservation — it never presses `u` or `<C-r>` in vim mode, never asserts the store's undo ran, and never exercises the `defaultVimHistory` fallthrough. Since CodeMirror's own history extension is now disabled, a broken routing here silently makes vim undo a no-op and nothing in the suite would fail.

findings.summary: The new 'fold setLocalSelection into the open batch' path in YorkieNoteStore is untested
findings.evidence: `setLocalSelection` gained a branch that publishes through `activeRoot`/`activePresence` when a batch is open, specifically to avoid a nested `doc.update` (which Yorkie rejects). No test in yorkie-note-store.test.ts calls `setLocalSelection` inside `store.batch(...)` (the file's only selection assertion is the pre-existing `getPeerSelections()` empty check), and the integration test cannot reach it either: noteSync's `batch()` closes synchronously inside its own plugin `update()` before the remote-selection plugin's `update()` calls `setLocalSelection`. So both the fold branch and the crash it guards against are uncovered.

findings.summary: `runHistory`'s toolbar refresh (selectionCb invocation after undo/redo) is not asserted anywhere
findings.evidence: `runHistory` deliberately calls `selectionCb?.(computeActiveFormats(view.state))` after `store[kind]()` because canUndo/canRedo now come from the store and the docChanged listener may not fire in time (notes-toolbar.tsx:193 re-reads them in that callback). No test registers `api.onSelectionChange(cb)` and asserts the callback fires on `api.undo()`/`api.redo()`; there is no notes-toolbar test file at all. Dropping that call would leave the undo/redo buttons stale and every test would still pass.

findings.summary: The `Mod-y` redo binding is never exercised
findings.evidence: historyKeymap adds three entries: Mod-z, Mod-y (mac: Mod-Shift-z) and Mod-Shift-z. editor.test.ts:107 presses only Ctrl-z and Ctrl-Shift-z; no test presses Ctrl-y, so the Windows/Linux redo binding could be missing or misbound without any failure.

findings.summary: Read-only 'history unbound' test has no positive control, so it can pass for the wrong reason
findings.evidence: The test dispatches a synthetic Ctrl-z keydown on a read-only mount and asserts the text is unchanged. Unlike the sibling keybinding test (editor.test.ts:119) it omits `keyCode`, and it never demonstrates that a keydown dispatched on this particular (non-focused, contenteditable=false) mount would reach a CodeMirror binding at all. If key delivery is inert in this configuration for unrelated reasons, the assertion holds whether or not `historyKeymap` is actually `[]` for readOnly — i.e. it would not catch a regression that binds history on read-only mounts.

findings.summary: `NoteEditorAPI.undo()/redo()` are the only history entry points with no read-only gate, so an API caller on a viewer-role mount would issue Yorkie writes
findings.evidence: The change gates every other history entry point on read-only: `historyKeymap` is `readOnly ? [] : keymap.of([...])` (editor.ts:213) and the vim route checks `cm.cm6.state.facet(EditorView.editable)` before calling `store[kind]()` (editor.ts:52). The returned API methods do not: `undo: () => { runHistory('undo'); ... }` / `redo: () => { runHistory('redo'); ... }` (editor.ts:431-438) call `store.undo()/redo()` unconditionally, and `YorkieNoteStore.undo()` calls `this.doc.history.undo()` (packages/frontend/src/app/notes/yorkie-note-store.ts:98), which commits a `doc.update()` write to the shared document. `canUndo()` is not a permission check — it only compares stack depth against `undoFloor`. Attack path: any holder of the editor API on a viewer-role share mount (`shared-document.tsx:310` passes `readOnly` into `NotesView` → `initialize(..., readOnly, ...)`, notes-view.tsx:95) invoking `api.undo()` writes to the note. It is not reachable today — `NotesToolbar` renders the undo/redo buttons only when `canFormat = !readOnly && mode !== 'view'` (notes-toolbar.tsx:200,205) and `SharedNotesLayout` renders no toolbar at all — and a viewer's local undo stack should be empty because `ensureText()` is skipped for read-only (notes-view.tsx:91), which is why confidence is low. Impact if a caller is added: an unauthorized write; the client-side `readOnly` flag is the only effective control whenever the server-side Yorkie auth webhook is deployed in its default shadow mode (`YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE` !== 'true', yorkie-auth.controller.ts:86-105), where the deny decision is logged but the write is allowed through. Suggested fix: guard `runHistory` on `readOnly` (or on `view.state.facet(EditorView.editable)`) so all three entry points share one gate.
searchedFor: read packages/notes/src/view/editor.ts in full (readOnly usage, historyKeymap, returned API)
grep NotesView|NotesToolbar across packages/frontend/src to enumerate every mount site
read packages/backend/src/document/yorkie-auth.controller.ts for the server-side enforcement path

findings.summary: `routeVimHistoryToStore()` permanently mutates the shared third-party `CodeMirror.commands` table process-wide on first note mount
findings.evidence: `CodeMirror.commands.undo = route('undo')` / `.redo = route('redo')` (editor.ts:58-59) overwrite entries on the module singleton exported by `@replit/codemirror-vim`, once per page, and are never restored on `dispose()`. The replacement resolves an arbitrary view's `noteStoreFacet` (editor.ts:49) and calls `store[kind]()` — a write-capable operation — for any CodeMirror view in the page that happens to provide that facet. Today only packages/notes imports the vim adapter (grep `@replit/codemirror-vim` across the repo: only packages/notes/package.json and editor.ts), and the `EditorView.editable` check at editor.ts:52 limits it, so there is no cross-surface impact now. Hardening suggestion: scope the override to views that carry the facet by installing it from an extension, or restore the originals on the last dispose, so a future vim-using editor cannot inherit the note store's write path.
searchedFor: read packages/notes/src/view/note-sync.ts for the noteStoreFacet definition and default

findings.summary: Review could not run — Claude API/quota error: [POOL_EXHAUSTED] every credential in the pool was retired
History keybindings always return `true`, swallowing Mod-z / Mod-Shift-z even when there is nothing to undo/redo
findings.evidence: `historyKeymap` entries call `runHistory('undo'|'redo')` and unconditionally `return true`, with no `store.canUndo()`/`canRedo()` check. `@codemirror/commands`' `undo`/`redo` (which this block says it mirrors) return `false` when the history is empty, letting the key fall through to lower-precedence bindings and to the browser. Here a Cmd+Z on a note with nothing to undo — including the common case where the undo floor blocks it (`YorkieNoteStore.canUndo()` returns false while `doc.history.canUndo()` is true) — is consumed and does nothing, instead of falling through. Same for the two redo entries.

findings.summary: `store.batch()` is opened on every docChanged ViewUpdate, including purely remote ones, re-entering Yorkie's `doc.update` from inside Yorkie's own event dispatch
findings.evidence: `update()` now calls `this.store.batch(...)` before it knows whether any transaction survives the `Transaction.remote` / user-event filter. For `YorkieNoteStore` that unconditionally executes `this.doc.update(...)` (yorkie-note-store.ts:78) while the store is still inside the `doc.subscribe` callback that produced the remote/undoredo change (subscribeRemote -> applyRemote -> view.dispatch -> plugin update). This works only because the batch happens to be empty; if any extension ever contributes a non-remote transaction to such an update (or a future store does work in `batch()` regardless of edits), a real local change would be created mid-publish. The cheap fix is to compute the qualifying transactions first and only open the batch when there is at least one edit to send.

findings.summary: `undoFloor` compared against a Yorkie undo stack that is capped and shifted, so the floor goes stale after enough local changes
findings.evidence: `canUndo()` gates on `doc.getUndoStackForTest().length > this.undoFloor`, treating the stack index as stable. Yorkie's `History.pushUndo` drops the oldest entry once the stack reaches its max depth (MaxUndoRedoStackDepth), so after that many local changes the entry the floor was meant to protect is no longer at index `undoFloor` — the comparison then blocks the user's oldest *legitimate* undo (stack length equals the floor while every remaining entry is a real edit). Same shape as the existing docs/slides stores, so possibly pre-existing, but it is newly introduced for notes here.

findings.summary: The presence-fold path in `setLocalSelection` is unreachable, and its "presence is not added to history" premise is doubtful
findings.evidence: `if (this.activeRoot && this.activePresence) publish(...)` only fires while a top-level `batch()`'s `doc.update` is open. The only caller of `setLocalSelection` is `NoteRemoteSelectionsPluginValue.update()` (packages/notes/src/view/remote-selection.ts:115), and that plugin is registered after `noteSync` (editor.ts:301 vs 303), so its `update()` always runs after `noteSync`'s batch has closed — `activeRoot` is null by then. Dead branch. Additionally, the doc comment at line 34 asserts presence never pollutes the undo unit; Yorkie appends a reverse-presence op to the change's reverse ops, so if this branch ever did fire, undoing that batch would also revert the local selection presence.

findings.summary: Undo/redo no longer restore the cursor position, because the revert arrives as a remote-tagged transaction
findings.evidence: With CodeMirror history removed (`basicSetup({history:false})`), the reverted text comes back via `store` -> `subscribeRemote` -> `NoteSyncPluginValue.applyRemote`, which dispatches with only `changes` and no `selection`. CodeMirror merely maps the existing selection through the change, so after Cmd+Z the caret stays wherever it was rather than moving to the reverted region — and for `MemNoteStore`, whose undo emits a whole-document `replace` (memory.ts:59, note-sync.ts:33), the selection collapses to the mapped position of a full-document replacement. This is a user-visible behavioural regression versus `@codemirror/commands`' undo.

findings.summary: `editText` is the only document accessor that does not null-check `root.content`, so a note whose `content` was removed crashes on the next keystroke
findings.evidence: `getText()` (line 53), `setLocalSelection()` (line 174) and `getPeerSelections()` (line 198) all guard `content` being absent, and `subscribeRemote` explicitly handles the `remove` op on `$` (line 145) meaning the code anticipates `content` disappearing. `editText` calls `root.content.edit(from,to,insert)` with no guard, so after that path (or on a read-only mount, where notes-view.tsx:91 skips `ensureText`) a local edit throws a TypeError inside the batch's `doc.update`; Yorkie then discards its clone and CodeMirror disables the crashed plugin, silently desyncing view and model.

findings.summary: `defaultVimHistory` captures `CodeMirror.commands.undo/redo` at module load and calls them unchecked on the fallthrough path
findings.evidence: `const defaultVimHistory = { undo: CodeMirror.commands.undo, redo: CodeMirror.commands.redo }` runs at import time; `route()` then calls `defaultVimHistory[kind](cm)` whenever the store is missing or the view is not editable. If `@replit/codemirror-vim` does not have those entries populated on `CodeMirror.commands` at import (or a later import re-assigns them), the captured value is `undefined` and pressing `u` in a read-only vim-mode note throws `TypeError: defaultVimHistory[kind] is not a function`. A `?.` call (or resolving `CodeMirror.commands[kind]` lazily) would make the fallthrough safe; no test in the change exercises the vim `u` / `<C-r>` route at all.

findings.summary: `routeVimHistoryToStore()` permanently monkey-patches the shared `@replit/codemirror-vim` module singleton (`CodeMirror.commands.undo/redo`) the first time any note editor mounts, and never restores it. This is a process-global side effect reaching out of `@wafflebase/notes` into a third-party module's static state; any other CodeMirror+vim editor in the app inherits the patched commands (they fall through via the `noteStoreFacet` guard today, but the coupling is invisible and order-dependent — behaviour now depends on whether a note has ever been mounted). A view-plugin/keymap-level override scoped to the note EditorView (or `Vim.defineAction`/`mapCommand` on the note's own extension set) would keep the hook inside the editor instance instead of the module. The task doc calls this "the supported-shaped hook", but nothing in the change verifies that no other editor package uses this module.

mergedFrom.summary: Vim's `:undo` / `:redo` ex-commands become silent no-ops after this change (basicSetup's `history` is off and the ex-command handlers were snapshotted at module load). That is a user-visible regression of an existing shipped feature (vim mode), disclosed only in the design doc and the task doc's "Out of scope" list — the originating issue never asked to drop it. `@replit/codemirror-vim` exposes `Vim.defineEx('undo', 'u', handler)` for exactly this kind of re-binding, so the claim that they "cannot be re-routed" (docs/design/notes/notes.md:300) may be wrong; if it is, the regression is avoidable rather than inherent.

findings.summary: `update()` now opens `store.batch()` — i.e. a real `doc.update()` on the Yorkie document — for EVERY docChanged ViewUpdate, including updates whose transactions are all `remote`-annotated (a peer's edit, or the editor re-applying the result of our own `doc.history.undo()`). That means a re-entrant `doc.update()` is opened while Yorkie is still dispatching its own change event, purely to run an empty body. A cheap guard (`if (update.transactions.every(tr => tr.annotation(Transaction.remote))) return;` before batching, or making `YorkieNoteStore.batch` lazy about opening the update) would keep the CRDT out of the remote path entirely instead of relying on "an empty doc.update pushes nothing".

`undoFloor` is captured once as an absolute stack length at construction and compared with `getUndoStackForTest().length > undoFloor` forever. Yorkie trims/clears the local undo stack (snapshots, `clearHistory()`), so after a snapshot in a long collaborative session the live stack can sit at or below a stale baseline and `canUndo()` would report false even though there are local units to revert — undo silently dies for the rest of the session. `YorkieDocStore` re-captures its floor (yorkie-doc-store.ts:732) and `YorkieSlidesStore` exposes `markUndoBaseline()`; the notes store has neither re-capture hook nor a test for the post-snapshot case.

The read-only policy is applied inconsistently: `historyKeymap` is `[]` on a read-only mount and the vim route checks `EditorView.editable` before delegating, but `NoteEditorAPI.undo()/redo()` (the toolbar/host entry point) call `store[kind]()` unconditionally. A read-only viewer that reaches the API — the toolbar hides the buttons today, but the API is exported to hosts — would attempt a Yorkie write the auth webhook must reject. The same `readOnly` flag that suppresses the keymap should gate `runHistory`.

Undo granularity regresses from CodeMirror's time-window keystroke grouping (`newGroupDelay`) to one unit per CodeMirror transaction, i.e. roughly per keystroke, in what is primarily a plain-text markdown editor. The issue asked only for CRDT-semantics undo; it did not ask to drop grouping, and the Docs/Slides precedent is weaker here because those are structured editors where a transaction is already a meaningful user action. The change discloses this (design doc) and the task plan declares coalescing out of scope, but nothing in the diff mitigates it (e.g. coalescing consecutive `input.type` ViewUpdates into one batch).

This is the fourth hand-rolled copy of the same ambient-root + `withUpdate` + `batchDepth` + `undoFloor` machinery (`yorkie-doc-store.ts`, `yorkie-slides-store.ts`, `yorkie-board-store.ts`, now `yorkie-note-store.ts`). The repo's stated expectation is reuse via `@wafflebase/core`, and I found no undo/batch helper there at all — so each store re-derives (and can re-get-wrong) the same invariants. Copying the pattern is what the issue asked for, so this is a preference, but the fourth copy is the natural moment to extract a shared `YorkieBatchHistory` mixin/helper.

mergedFrom.summary: Production code depends on the SDK's explicitly test-only API `doc.getUndoStackForTest()` for the undo floor. Pre-existing repo pattern (docs/slides/board do the same), so not introduced here, but each new site deepens the dependency on an API the SDK is free to remove.

findings.summary: The paired task plan still has every checkbox unticked and `PR: (to be filled after opening)`, while the design doc already marks the feature "shipped". CONTRIBUTING has the archive step happen at merge, so this is only a pre-merge tidiness note — but the plan as committed reads as not-yet-started for a change that is complete.

+# Notes native undo — lessons (issue #604)
+
+## Context
+
+Migrate WaffleNotes undo/redo from CodeMirror local history to Yorkie
+`doc.history`, so undo preserves peers' concurrent edits.
+
+## Lessons
+
+- The issue's prerequisite spike resolved cleanly: `Text.edit()` reverse
+  ops are supported on `@yorkie-js/sdk` 0.7.13. The `Tree.editByPath`
+  merge caveat that motivated the spike is a Tree-only limitation and
+  never applied to notes, whose whole content is one `Text`.
+- An empty `doc.update()` pushes nothing onto the undo stack, so
+  `batch()` does not need to pre-check whether the body will mutate.
+- Disabling `basicSetup`'s `history()` silently breaks vim's `u` /
+  `<C-r>` too: `@replit/codemirror-vim` routes them through
+  `CodeMirror.commands.undo/redo`, which call `@codemirror/commands`'
+  `undo(view)` and no-op without the history extension. The static
+  `CodeMirror.commands` map is read at call time, so overriding it is
+  the supported-shaped hook; its `:undo` ex-command copy is snapshotted
+  at module load and cannot be re-routed.
+- Undo granularity changes: CM history groups keystrokes by time
+  (`newGroupDelay`), Yorkie's unit is one change. One CM transaction =
+  one undo unit, so undo now steps per keystroke — the same behavior
+  Docs and Slides already have after their migrations.

+# Notes native undo — migrate to Yorkie `doc.history` (issue #604)
+
+PR: (to be filled after opening)
+
+## Goal
+
+Move WaffleNotes undo/redo off CodeMirror's local history onto
+Yorkie-native undo (`doc.history`), so undo carries CRDT semantics and
+preserves a peer's concurrent edits instead of last-write-wins-ing over
+them. Reuses the pattern already shipped in Slides
+(`docs/design/slides/slides-native-undo.md`) and Docs
+(`packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts`).
+
+## Prerequisite spike (done — result recorded here)
+
+Verified against the pinned `@yorkie-js/sdk` 0.7.13 that character-level
+`Text.edit()` **is** reversible through `doc.history`:
+
+- Two `content.edit()` calls inside ONE `doc.update()` push exactly one
+  undo-stack entry; `history.undo()` reverts both, `redo()` re-applies.
+- The undo emits a `local-change` event with `source === 'undoredo'`
+  carrying `edit` ops on `$.content` with correct `from`/`to`/`content`
+  (already reversed in apply order), i.e. the dormant `isUndoRedo` path
+  in `yorkie-note-store.ts` receives exactly what it needs.
+- A `doc.update()` whose body mutates nothing pushes **no** undo entry,
+  so an empty batch is free.
+
+(`Tree.editByPath` merge non-reversibility, called out in the issue,
+does not apply — notes store markdown in a single `Text`.)
+
+## Approach
+
+**Store layer (`packages/notes/src/store/store.ts`)** — extend
+`NoteStore` with `batch(fn)`, `undo()`, `redo()`, `canUndo()`,
+`canRedo()`. Undo becomes store-owned (like `DocStore`/`SlidesStore`)
+rather than view-owned.
+
+**`YorkieNoteStore`** — ambient-root + `withUpdate()`: a top-level
+`batch()` opens ONE `doc.update()` and every `editText()` runs against
+that ambient root, so one CodeMirror transaction group = one Yorkie
+change = one undo unit. `setLocalSelection` folds into the batch's
+ambient presence proxy when a batch is open. `undo()/redo()` delegate to
+`doc.history`, gated by an undo floor captured at construction (after
+`ensureText()` seeding) so a user cannot undo the seed away.
+
+**`MemNoteStore`** — snapshot-based local history so the engine still
+has working undo without a CRDT (tests / non-collaborative use). Undo
+emits a `replace` remote change so the view reflects it, mirroring how
+the Yorkie store's undo comes back through `subscribeRemote`.
+
+**`note-sync.ts`** — wrap the per-`ViewUpdate` `editText` loop in
+`store.batch()`.
+
+**`editor.ts`** — `basicSetup({ history: false, historyKeymap: false })`;
+bind `Mod-z` / `Mod-Shift-z` / `Mod-y` to the store (skipped in
+read-only); `NoteEditorAPI.undo/redo/canUndo/canRedo` delegate to the
+store. Vim's `u` / `<C-r>` go through `CodeMirror.commands.undo/redo`,
+which the vim adapter looks up at call time — override them once to
+route to the note store resolved from the view's `noteStoreFacet`, else
+vim undo would silently no-op with CM history disabled.
+
+## Tasks
+
+- [ ] `NoteStore`: `batch` / `undo` / `redo` / `canUndo` / `canRedo`
+- [ ] `MemNoteStore`: snapshot history + `replace` emission on undo/redo
+- [ ] `YorkieNoteStore`: ambient root, `withUpdate`, batch, undo floor,
+      `doc.history` delegation
+- [ ] `note-sync.ts`: wrap local edits in `store.batch()`
+- [ ] `editor.ts`: disable CM history, history keymap → store, API
+      delegation, vim command routing
+- [ ] Tests: batch grouping = 1 undo unit, undo floor, peer-edit
+      preservation (churn regression), no-echo on undo, MemNoteStore
+      history, engine-level keybinding
+- [ ] `docs/design/notes/notes.md`: Yorkie-native undo section
+
+## Out of scope
+
+- Time-based keystroke coalescing (Yorkie's undo unit is the change;
+  Docs and Slides behave the same way).
+- `:undo` / `:redo` ex-commands in vim (the vim package snapshots those
+  handlers at module load, so they cannot be re-routed).

verdict.reason: The claimed code exists as described: packages/notes/src/view/editor.ts:38-60 defines `defaultVimHistory` and `routeVimHistoryToStore()`, which globally replace `CodeMirror.commands.undo/redo` with a store-routing closure plus a read-only/facet-missing fallthrough, invoked from `initialize()` at editor.ts:137. No test anywhere exercises it. editor.test.ts's only vim test (lines 156-172) asserts just `getKeymap()` and text preservation; its history tests (lines 60-154) use `api.undo()` and Ctrl-z in default keymap, never `CodeMirror.commands`. The frontend integration test packages/frontend/src/app/notes/notes-undo-integration.test.ts mounts the real editor over a real Yorkie store but only drives `api.insertTable()/undo()/redo()` and never enables vim. A repo-wide case-insensitive grep for `\bvim\b` returns 19 files with editor.test.ts as the sole test file, and `@replit/codemirror-vim` is imported in exactly one file (editor.ts:5), so no test can reach the replaced commands. Since CodeMirror's history extension is disabled, broken routing would silently no-op vim undo with nothing failing — a real behavior change with zero meaningful coverage (major under the test-adequacy rubric).

finding.evidence: `setLocalSelection` gained a branch that publishes through `activeRoot`/`activePresence` when a batch is open, specifically to avoid a nested `doc.update` (which Yorkie rejects). No test in yorkie-note-store.test.ts calls `setLocalSelection` inside `store.batch(...)` (the file's only selection assertion is the pre-existing `getPeerSelections()` empty check), and the integration test cannot reach it either: noteSync's `batch()` closes synchronously inside its own plugin `update()` before the remote-selection plugin's `update()` calls `setLocalSelection`. So both the fold branch and the crash it guards against are uncovered.

verdict.reason: The fold branch in YorkieNoteStore.setLocalSelection (yorkie-note-store.ts:187-193, publishing via activeRoot/activePresence when a batch is open instead of opening a nested doc.update) has no test. The only two files referencing YorkieNoteStore are yorkie-note-store.test.ts — which never calls setLocalSelection anywhere (its batches at lines 65, 84, 97, 114, 130 contain only editText; the sole selection assertion is the pre-existing getPeerSelections() empty check at line 57) — and notes-undo-integration.test.ts, which asserts only text and undo-stack state and structurally cannot reach the branch: noteSync is registered before noteRemoteSelections (editor.ts:301-303) and its update() opens and closes store.batch() synchronously (note-sync.ts:61-77) before the remote-selection plugin calls setLocalSelection (remote-selection.ts:109-118), so activeRoot is null. The other test call sites of setLocalSelection are fake stores whose batch is `(fn) => fn()` (note-sync.test.ts:19, remote-selection.test.ts:13-19) or MemNoteStore (memory.test.ts:84), neither of which exercises the Yorkie nesting guard. No packages/frontend/tests notes suite and no e2e directory exist. This is a new behavior branch shipped with no meaningful test — in-lane "missing tests", major.

samples.summary: `NoteEditorAPI.undo()/redo()` are the only history entry points with no read-only gate, so an API caller on a viewer-role mount would issue Yorkie writes
samples.evidence: The change gates every other history entry point on read-only: `historyKeymap` is `readOnly ? [] : keymap.of([...])` (editor.ts:213) and the vim route checks `cm.cm6.state.facet(EditorView.editable)` before calling `store[kind]()` (editor.ts:52). The returned API methods do not: `undo: () => { runHistory('undo'); ... }` / `redo: () => { runHistory('redo'); ... }` (editor.ts:431-438) call `store.undo()/redo()` unconditionally, and `YorkieNoteStore.undo()` calls `this.doc.history.undo()` (packages/frontend/src/app/notes/yorkie-note-store.ts:98), which commits a `doc.update()` write to the shared document. `canUndo()` is not a permission check — it only compares stack depth against `undoFloor`. Attack path: any holder of the editor API on a viewer-role share mount (`shared-document.tsx:310` passes `readOnly` into `NotesView` → `initialize(..., readOnly, ...)`, notes-view.tsx:95) invoking `api.undo()` writes to the note. It is not reachable today — `NotesToolbar` renders the undo/redo buttons only when `canFormat = !readOnly && mode !== 'view'` (notes-toolbar.tsx:200,205) and `SharedNotesLayout` renders no toolbar at all — and a viewer's local undo stack should be empty because `ensureText()` is skipped for read-only (notes-view.tsx:91), which is why confidence is low. Impact if a caller is added: an unauthorized write; the client-side `readOnly` flag is the only effective control whenever the server-side Yorkie auth webhook is deployed in its default shadow mode (`YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE` !== 'true', yorkie-auth.controller.ts:86-105), where the deny decision is logged but the write is allowed through. Suggested fix: guard `runHistory` on `readOnly` (or on `view.state.facet(EditorView.editable)`) so all three entry points share one gate.

read packages/backend/src/document/yorkie-auth.controller.ts for the server-side enforcement path

samples.summary: `routeVimHistoryToStore()` permanently mutates the shared third-party `CodeMirror.commands` table process-wide on first note mount
samples.evidence: `CodeMirror.commands.undo = route('undo')` / `.redo = route('redo')` (editor.ts:58-59) overwrite entries on the module singleton exported by `@replit/codemirror-vim`, once per page, and are never restored on `dispose()`. The replacement resolves an arbitrary view's `noteStoreFacet` (editor.ts:49) and calls `store[kind]()` — a write-capable operation — for any CodeMirror view in the page that happens to provide that facet. Today only packages/notes imports the vim adapter (grep `@replit/codemirror-vim` across the repo: only packages/notes/package.json and editor.ts), and the `EditorView.editable` check at editor.ts:52 limits it, so there is no cross-surface impact now. Hardening suggestion: scope the override to views that carry the facet by installing it from an extension, or restore the originals on the last dispose, so a future vim-using editor cannot inherit the note store's write path.

samples.summary: History keybindings always return `true`, swallowing Mod-z / Mod-Shift-z even when there is nothing to undo/redo
samples.evidence: `historyKeymap` entries call `runHistory('undo'|'redo')` and unconditionally `return true`, with no `store.canUndo()`/`canRedo()` check. `@codemirror/commands`' `undo`/`redo` (which this block says it mirrors) return `false` when the history is empty, letting the key fall through to lower-precedence bindings and to the browser. Here a Cmd+Z on a note with nothing to undo — including the common case where the undo floor blocks it (`YorkieNoteStore.canUndo()` returns false while `doc.history.canUndo()` is true) — is consumed and does nothing, instead of falling through. Same for the two redo entries.

samples.summary: `store.batch()` is opened on every docChanged ViewUpdate, including purely remote ones, re-entering Yorkie's `doc.update` from inside Yorkie's own event dispatch
samples.evidence: `update()` now calls `this.store.batch(...)` before it knows whether any transaction survives the `Transaction.remote` / user-event filter. For `YorkieNoteStore` that unconditionally executes `this.doc.update(...)` (yorkie-note-store.ts:78) while the store is still inside the `doc.subscribe` callback that produced the remote/undoredo change (subscribeRemote -> applyRemote -> view.dispatch -> plugin update). This works only because the batch happens to be empty; if any extension ever contributes a non-remote transaction to such an update (or a future store does work in `batch()` regardless of edits), a real local change would be created mid-publish. The cheap fix is to compute the qualifying transactions first and only open the batch when there is at least one edit to send.

samples.summary: `undoFloor` compared against a Yorkie undo stack that is capped and shifted, so the floor goes stale after enough local changes
samples.evidence: `canUndo()` gates on `doc.getUndoStackForTest().length > this.undoFloor`, treating the stack index as stable. Yorkie's `History.pushUndo` drops the oldest entry once the stack reaches its max depth (MaxUndoRedoStackDepth), so after that many local changes the entry the floor was meant to protect is no longer at index `undoFloor` — the comparison then blocks the user's oldest *legitimate* undo (stack length equals the floor while every remaining entry is a real edit). Same shape as the existing docs/slides stores, so possibly pre-existing, but it is newly introduced for notes here.

samples.summary: The presence-fold path in `setLocalSelection` is unreachable, and its "presence is not added to history" premise is doubtful
samples.evidence: `if (this.activeRoot && this.activePresence) publish(...)` only fires while a top-level `batch()`'s `doc.update` is open. The only caller of `setLocalSelection` is `NoteRemoteSelectionsPluginValue.update()` (packages/notes/src/view/remote-selection.ts:115), and that plugin is registered after `noteSync` (editor.ts:301 vs 303), so its `update()` always runs after `noteSync`'s batch has closed — `activeRoot` is null by then. Dead branch. Additionally, the doc comment at line 34 asserts presence never pollutes the undo unit; Yorkie appends a reverse-presence op to the change's reverse ops, so if this branch ever did fire, undoing that batch would also revert the local selection presence.

samples.summary: Undo/redo no longer restore the cursor position, because the revert arrives as a remote-tagged transaction
samples.evidence: With CodeMirror history removed (`basicSetup({history:false})`), the reverted text comes back via `store` -> `subscribeRemote` -> `NoteSyncPluginValue.applyRemote`, which dispatches with only `changes` and no `selection`. CodeMirror merely maps the existing selection through the change, so after Cmd+Z the caret stays wherever it was rather than moving to the reverted region — and for `MemNoteStore`, whose undo emits a whole-document `replace` (memory.ts:59, note-sync.ts:33), the selection collapses to the mapped position of a full-document replacement. This is a user-visible behavioural regression versus `@codemirror/commands`' undo.

samples.summary: `editText` is the only document accessor that does not null-check `root.content`, so a note whose `content` was removed crashes on the next keystroke
samples.evidence: `getText()` (line 53), `setLocalSelection()` (line 174) and `getPeerSelections()` (line 198) all guard `content` being absent, and `subscribeRemote` explicitly handles the `remove` op on `$` (line 145) meaning the code anticipates `content` disappearing. `editText` calls `root.content.edit(from,to,insert)` with no guard, so after that path (or on a read-only mount, where notes-view.tsx:91 skips `ensureText`) a local edit throws a TypeError inside the batch's `doc.update`; Yorkie then discards its clone and CodeMirror disables the crashed plugin, silently desyncing view and model.

samples.summary: `defaultVimHistory` captures `CodeMirror.commands.undo/redo` at module load and calls them unchecked on the fallthrough path
samples.evidence: `const defaultVimHistory = { undo: CodeMirror.commands.undo, redo: CodeMirror.commands.redo }` runs at import time; `route()` then calls `defaultVimHistory[kind](cm)` whenever the store is missing or the view is not editable. If `@replit/codemirror-vim` does not have those entries populated on `CodeMirror.commands` at import (or a later import re-assigns them), the captured value is `undefined` and pressing `u` in a read-only vim-mode note throws `TypeError: defaultVimHistory[kind] is not a function`. A `?.` call (or resolving `CodeMirror.commands[kind]` lazily) would make the fallthrough safe; no test in the change exercises the vim `u` / `<C-r>` route at all.

finding.summary: `editText` is the only document accessor that does not null-check `root.content`, so a note whose `content` was removed crashes on the next keystroke
finding.evidence: `getText()` (line 53), `setLocalSelection()` (line 174) and `getPeerSelections()` (line 198) all guard `content` being absent, and `subscribeRemote` explicitly handles the `remove` op on `$` (line 145) meaning the code anticipates `content` disappearing. `editText` calls `root.content.edit(from,to,insert)` with no guard, so after that path (or on a read-only mount, where notes-view.tsx:91 skips `ensureText`) a local edit throws a TypeError inside the batch's `doc.update`; Yorkie then discards its clone and CodeMirror disables the crashed plugin, silently desyncing view and model.

verdict.reason: The claimed code is present exactly as described. yorkie-note-store.ts:57-61 calls root.content.edit(from,to,insert) with no guard, while every sibling accessor guards content: getText() (52-55, `content ? content.toString() : ''`), setLocalSelection() (173-179, `if (head === null || !content)`) and getPeerSelections() (197-198, `if (!content) return []`). The unseeded-document path is also real: notes-view.tsx:91 runs `if (!readOnly) ensureText(doc)` and ensureText's own comment (lines 38-40) states it must only be invoked on a writable document, so a read-only mount (shared-document.tsx:310) can carry a doc whose root.content is missing or is a mis-materialized plain {context,text} object without `.edit` — precisely the shape ensureText (47-50) and the backend (note-content.ts:43, :63) defend against. I could not close reachability: editor.ts:287 sets only EditorView.editable.of(!readOnly) and never EditorState.readOnly, so keymap commands (indentWithTab, editor.ts:251) and the programmatic API (toggleBold/insertTable, editor.ts:426-430) still dispatch doc changes that note-sync.ts:73 routes into store.editText; notes-view.tsx:108 also omits readOnly/viewMode from the effect deps while the viewMode effect (118-120) can un-hide the pane of a read-only-initialized editor. The reviewer's secondary rationale is weaker than claimed (nothing in the repo deletes root.content; writeNoteRoot at note-content.ts:61-68 replaces it, and the remove-on-$ branch at yorkie-note-store.ts:144-151 is commented as a *replacement* reload), but that does not refute the missing guard itself. A TypeError inside doc.update is a runtime crash in the correctness lane, and I cannot cite a guard that makes it unreachable, so the finding stands.

finding.summary: `defaultVimHistory` captures `CodeMirror.commands.undo/redo` at module load and calls them unchecked on the fallthrough path
finding.evidence: `const defaultVimHistory = { undo: CodeMirror.commands.undo, redo: CodeMirror.commands.redo }` runs at import time; `route()` then calls `defaultVimHistory[kind](cm)` whenever the store is missing or the view is not editable. If `@replit/codemirror-vim` does not have those entries populated on `CodeMirror.commands` at import (or a later import re-assigns them), the captured value is `undefined` and pressing `u` in a read-only vim-mode note throws `TypeError: defaultVimHistory[kind] is not a function`. A `?.` call (or resolving `CodeMirror.commands[kind]` lazily) would make the fallthrough safe; no test in the change exercises the vim `u` / `<C-r>` route at all.

verdict.reason: The code is present exactly as described: packages/notes/src/view/editor.ts:38-41 captures CodeMirror.commands.undo/redo into a module-scope const at import time (immediately after the import at line 5), and line 56 calls defaultVimHistory[kind](cm) with no optional-call or existence check on the fallthrough path. The fallthrough is reachable on a real path: it fires whenever the store is missing or EditorView.editable is false, and read-only mounts exist (initialize's readOnly param -> EditorView.editable.of(!readOnly) at line 287; read-only mounts exercised at editor.test.ts:28 and :145) while vim mode is switchable at runtime (setKeymap('vim') -> vim() extension, lines 247-248, tested at editor.test.ts:156-165). So a read-only note in vim mode pressing `u` reaches line 56. No test exercises the vim u / <C-r> route at all. I could not refute the premise: node_modules is not installed in this worktree (globs for **/node_modules/@replit/** and **/cm_adapter* return nothing), so I cannot verify whether @replit/codemirror-vim 6.3.0 populates commands.undo/redo at module evaluation. tsconfig has strict:true but not noUncheckedIndexedAccess (packages/notes/tsconfig.json:13), so an index-signature type would compile fine even if the runtime value were undefined -- the type system gives no protection. The only repo-internal support for the entries being populated is prose authored by this same change (docs/design/notes/notes.md:300-302, docs/tasks/active/20260730-notes-native-undo-lessons.md:19-22), which is not citable code and not a guard. My prior is that the library does populate them, making the crash unlikely to fire, but that is doubt about the premise rather than a concrete refutation, so the finding stays with low confidence.

samples.summary: `routeVimHistoryToStore()` permanently monkey-patches the shared `@replit/codemirror-vim` module singleton (`CodeMirror.commands.undo/redo`) the first time any note editor mounts, and never restores it. This is a process-global side effect reaching out of `@wafflebase/notes` into a third-party module's static state; any other CodeMirror+vim editor in the app inherits the patched commands (they fall through via the `noteStoreFacet` guard today, but the coupling is invisible and order-dependent — behaviour now depends on whether a note has ever been mounted). A view-plugin/keymap-level override scoped to the note EditorView (or `Vim.defineAction`/`mapCommand` on the note's own extension set) would keep the hook inside the editor instance instead of the module. The task doc calls this "the supported-shaped hook", but nothing in the change verifies that no other editor package uses this module.

Vim's `:undo` / `:redo` ex-commands become silent no-ops after this change (basicSetup's `history` is off and the ex-command handlers were snapshotted at module load). That is a user-visible regression of an existing shipped feature (vim mode), disclosed only in the design doc and the task doc's "Out of scope" list — the originating issue never asked to drop it. `@replit/codemirror-vim` exposes `Vim.defineEx('undo', 'u', handler)` for exactly this kind of re-binding, so the claim that they "cannot be re-routed" (docs/design/notes/notes.md:300) may be wrong; if it is, the regression is avoidable rather than inherent.

`update()` now opens `store.batch()` — i.e. a real `doc.update()` on the Yorkie document — for EVERY docChanged ViewUpdate, including updates whose transactions are all `remote`-annotated (a peer's edit, or the editor re-applying the result of our own `doc.history.undo()`). That means a re-entrant `doc.update()` is opened while Yorkie is still dispatching its own change event, purely to run an empty body. A cheap guard (`if (update.transactions.every(tr => tr.annotation(Transaction.remote))) return;` before batching, or making `YorkieNoteStore.batch` lazy about opening the update) would keep the CRDT out of the remote path entirely instead of relying on "an empty doc.update pushes nothing".

`undoFloor` is captured once as an absolute stack length at construction and compared with `getUndoStackForTest().length > undoFloor` forever. Yorkie trims/clears the local undo stack (snapshots, `clearHistory()`), so after a snapshot in a long collaborative session the live stack can sit at or below a stale baseline and `canUndo()` would report false even though there are local units to revert — undo silently dies for the rest of the session. `YorkieDocStore` re-captures its floor (yorkie-doc-store.ts:732) and `YorkieSlidesStore` exposes `markUndoBaseline()`; the notes store has neither re-capture hook nor a test for the post-snapshot case.

The read-only policy is applied inconsistently: `historyKeymap` is `[]` on a read-only mount and the vim route checks `EditorView.editable` before delegating, but `NoteEditorAPI.undo()/redo()` (the toolbar/host entry point) call `store[kind]()` unconditionally. A read-only viewer that reaches the API — the toolbar hides the buttons today, but the API is exported to hosts — would attempt a Yorkie write the auth webhook must reject. The same `readOnly` flag that suppresses the keymap should gate `runHistory`.

Undo granularity regresses from CodeMirror's time-window keystroke grouping (`newGroupDelay`) to one unit per CodeMirror transaction, i.e. roughly per keystroke, in what is primarily a plain-text markdown editor. The issue asked only for CRDT-semantics undo; it did not ask to drop grouping, and the Docs/Slides precedent is weaker here because those are structured editors where a transaction is already a meaningful user action. The change discloses this (design doc) and the task plan declares coalescing out of scope, but nothing in the diff mitigates it (e.g. coalescing consecutive `input.type` ViewUpdates into one batch).

This is the fourth hand-rolled copy of the same ambient-root + `withUpdate` + `batchDepth` + `undoFloor` machinery (`yorkie-doc-store.ts`, `yorkie-slides-store.ts`, `yorkie-board-store.ts`, now `yorkie-note-store.ts`). The repo's stated expectation is reuse via `@wafflebase/core`, and I found no undo/batch helper there at all — so each store re-derives (and can re-get-wrong) the same invariants. Copying the pattern is what the issue asked for, so this is a preference, but the fourth copy is the natural moment to extract a shared `YorkieBatchHistory` mixin/helper.

Production code depends on the SDK's explicitly test-only API `doc.getUndoStackForTest()` for the undo floor. Pre-existing repo pattern (docs/slides/board do the same), so not introduced here, but each new site deepens the dependency on an API the SDK is free to remove.

The paired task plan still has every checkbox unticked and `PR: (to be filled after opening)`, while the design doc already marks the feature "shipped". CONTRIBUTING has the archive step happen at merge, so this is only a pre-merge tidiness note — but the plan as committed reads as not-yet-started for a change that is complete.
